spark.title: Graph Databases & Traversal Engines
spark.summary: Store and traverse deeply connected entities in O(1) per hop using index-free adjacency, avoiding the exponential JOIN explosion of relational databases.
spark.keyTakeaway: Graph databases excel at multi-hop relationship queries (friends-of-friends, fraud rings, dependency graphs) because each vertex stores direct physical pointers to its adjacent edges.
spark.byteSummary:
Store and traverse deeply connected entities in O(1) per hop using index-free adjacency, avoiding the exponential JOIN explosion of relational databases.

A 4-hop "friends-of-friends" or "fraud ring" query in an RDBMS requires 4 self-JOINs over millions of rows, causing latency to explode exponentially.

Graph databases excel at multi-hop relationship queries (friends-of-friends, fraud rings, dependency graphs) because each vertex stores direct physical pointers to its adjacent edges.

concept.whyItMatters: A 4-hop "friends-of-friends" or "fraud ring" query in an RDBMS requires 4 self-JOINs over millions of rows, causing latency to explode exponentially. Native [graph databases](/domains/nosql) use index-free adjacency so traversal cost depends only on the local neighborhood size, not total graph size.
whenToUse: Social networks, recommendation engines, real-time fraud ring detection, and knowledge/dependency graphs (3+ hop traversals).
Schemas where relationships carry rich properties (weights, timestamps, roles) and evolve frequently.
whenNotToUse: High-volume flat event logs, time-series metrics, or global full-table analytical aggregations (use columnar/time-series stores instead).
keyPoints: Property Graph model: Nodes (vertices) with labels & key-value properties, connected by directed typed Edges (relationships) with properties.
Index-free adjacency: each node physically points to its incident edges in memory/disk—traversing an edge is an $O(1)$ pointer chase rather than an $O(\log N)$ B-tree index lookup.
Query languages: Cypher (`MATCH (a)-[:FOLLOWS*1..3]->(b)`), Gremlin (imperative traversal), and GraphQL-over-graph.
Scaling challenge: partitioning arbitrary graphs across shards without cutting hot edges (min-cut partitioning) is hard; many systems keep the graph topology in distributed RAM.

sections.content:
## Architecture & Trade-Off Matrix

| Hop Depth | RDBMS (Self-JOINs) | Native Graph DB (Index-Free Adjacency) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1 hop** | Fast ($O(\log N)$ index seek) | Fast ($O(1)$ pointer chase) |
| **2 hops** | Moderate (index join) | Fast ($O(d)$ local degree) |
| **3–5+ hops** | Severe degradation / timeouts | Linear in visited neighborhood |
| **Horizontal Sharding** | Standard key sharding | Hard (cross-shard edge hops) |

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
